CallerContext

Who the AXE site sees for one MCP caller over HTTP. Returned by ServeHttpOptions.clientFor for each verified caller.

Properties

client?
optional client?: ClientOptions;

AXE client options for this caller, merged over createMcpServer's client option, whose auth and headers are not inherited. For a URL or manifest source, set auth to a credential the AXE site accepts for this user (for example a token obtained by token exchange).

identity?
optional identity?: Identity | null;

In-process source only: the identity the AXE runtime uses for this caller, as a framework adapter would pass it. The site's authenticate is not consulted.

tenant?

In-process source only: the tenant, as a framework adapter would pass it.

McpServerOptions

Properties

apps?
optional apps?: boolean;

EXPERIMENTAL. Offer the MCP Apps view (ui://axe/presentation) for actions with display, only to a host that declared the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension. false turns it off. Default on.

client?
optional client?: ClientOptions;

Options for the underlying AXE client (auth, agent identification, fetch). Over HTTP with serveHttp, auth and headers here are one identity shared by every MCP client; see ServeHttpOptions.clientFor for per-caller identity.

elicitation?
optional elicitation?: 
  | boolean
  | {
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

MCP elicitation for the ladder, used only with a client that declared the elicitation capability (and a transport that can carry a server request: stdio, in-memory, or HTTP sessions, not stateless HTTP). A needs_input whose preferred kind is not sensitive and fits the form subset is asked for in a form and continued; a sensitive kind or a needs_human step is offered as the site's page in URL mode when the client supports it. false turns it off. Default: on, with timeoutMs 600000 (ten minutes) for the user to answer.

extraTools?
optional extraTools?: ExtraTool[];

Tools served beside the derived ones, answered by your own code with any MCP content (an image, say) instead of an AXE result. A name that a derived tool also uses is an error. Each call receives the request's verified authInfo (HTTP with auth) and the caller clientFor returned for it; over stdio both are absent. Identify the caller from them, never from the arguments.

name?
optional name?: string;

Server name reported to MCP clients. Defaults to the manifest name.

pollBudgetMs?
optional pollBudgetMs?: number;

How long pending results are polled inside a tool call before returning. Default 20000 ms.

version?
optional version?: string;

ServeHttpOptions

Properties

allowedOrigins?
optional allowedOrigins?: string[];

Browser origins allowed to call the endpoint, besides the endpoint's own. A request whose Origin is neither is refused with 403 (DNS rebinding protection).

allowSharedCredentials?
optional allowSharedCredentials?: boolean;

Allow createMcpServer's client.auth or client.headers to act for every HTTP caller. Default false: serveHttp refuses that configuration unless clientFor is given.

anonymousSessionClientFor?
optional anonymousSessionClientFor?: (sessionId) => MaybePromise<CallerContext>;

Give each unauthenticated stateful MCP session its own caller identity. This is for services that defer account login until a tool actually needs it: transport initialization stays anonymous, while the cryptographically random MCP session id isolates the later login and every page it can reach. Requires sessions and cannot be combined with transport auth or clientFor.

ToolCallContext

The MCP tool call an in-process AXE request is serving, passed as AxeLike.handle's third argument. It lets the in-process server ask the user something through the client, within the same tool call, in the same session and as the same caller (the relay asks for approvals this way). Absent outside a tool call and for a URL or manifest source.

Aborted when the client cancels the tool call or the connection closes.

Variables

APPS_EXTENSION

const APPS_EXTENSION: "io.modelcontextprotocol/ui" = "io.modelcontextprotocol/ui";

A minimal MCP Apps view for AXE display (review item 14, 2026-09-24). EXPERIMENTAL.

The installed MCP SDK (1.30.1) has no types for the Apps extension, so this module implements the wire shape from the extension's specification (SEP-1865, "MCP Apps", stable version 2026-01-26, read 2026-09-24 at github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps and apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io):

  • A host that renders Apps declares capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"] with mimeTypes including text/html;profile=mcp-app. Servers SHOULD check it before offering UI; the bridge offers nothing to a host that did not declare it.
  • A UI resource has a ui:// URI and that MIME type, and is read with resources/read (text). A tool points at it with _meta.ui.resourceUri.
  • The view is an iframe that speaks JSON-RPC over postMessage: it sends ui/initialize, then ui/notifications/initialized, and receives ui/notifications/tool-result with the tool's CallToolResult. The host's default CSP allows inline script and style and no network (connect-src 'none', images from 'self' and data: only).

The view here is one static page for every display action. Each ok result of such an action carries the toHTML rendering in _meta["axe/presentation"].html; the view parses it with DOMParser (which runs no script), drops scripts, event-handler attributes, the affordance buttons (they have no effect inside a host), and anything but the page's <style> and <main>, and shows it. The text content stays the Markdown rendering, which is what a host without Apps shows ([P-MCP-8]).

protectedResourceMetadata()

function protectedResourceMetadata(options): object;

RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata for an MCP endpoint, which MCP clients read to find the authorization server. Returns the document, the path and URL to serve it at (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource plus the endpoint's path), and a fetch handler for it. This package does not issue tokens.

toFormSchema()

function toFormSchema(schema): FormSchema | null;

The form subset of a payload schema, or null when any part of it has no form rendering (a nested object, an array of objects, a union, a reference). Keywords outside the subset that only narrow a value (a format other than the four, for instance) are dropped; the site validates the payload again on /axe/continue.
